data.name: Farag
data.gender_notes: Farag is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘faraghah’, meaning 'rare' or 'precious'. In Islamic culture, this name represents the uniqueness and value of every individual creation of Allah. The name Farag carries the meaning “Rare, precious, unique” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Farag usually hope their child will grow to embody rare, precious, unique and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with divine value and uniqueness.
data.etymology: Farag belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rare, precious, unique.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farag total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_pashto.name: فرج

historical_references.reference: Farag ibn al-Hadath was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad who is mentioned in various Hadiths. He was known for his generosity and was given the title 'Farag al-Awald' (Farag of the Sons) because of his kindness towards children.
historical_references.time_period: 610-632 AD (Pre-Islamic period to the Prophet's Death)
historical_references.context: Islamic History, Companions of the Prophet Muhammad

historical_references.reference: Farag ibn Barad is mentioned in the historical account of the Battle of Hunayn (630 AD) as one of the commanders of the Islamic army. He led a contingent of 3,000 men from Kufa against the enemy forces.
